mainEntity.name: Should I install a full kitchen or a kitchenette in a guest house?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full kitchen includes full-size cooking appliances, a standard refrigerator, extensive counter space, and dedicated 240-volt electrical circuits, whereas a kitchenette relies on compact, plug-in appliances. Kitchenettes typically feature a bar sink, under-counter refrigerator, microwave, and small counter area, requiring less plumbing infrastructure and simpler electrical wiring. Local zoning codes frequently dictate whether an accessory unit is permitted to have a full stove or range oven. Choosing a kitchenette reduces overall construction expenses and preserves interior square footage for living or bedroom areas.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchenette saves money and space while using standard 120-volt outlets; a full kitchen requires larger floor plans, 240-volt circuits, and zoning approval for full ranges.
